explanation: Two users interacting on the same system, at the same time, without interference.

tagline.text: Every system assumes a single user. Duo Input is the technology that changes that assumption and everything that follows from it.

info-1.title: Built for one. Used by two
info-1.paragraph1: Operating systems are built around one cursor. One input, one session, one person in control.
info-1.paragraph2: The moment a second user touches a second screen, the inputs collide. The cursor jumps. Control goes to whoever touched last.
info-1.paragraph3: It's not a bug. It's the default, and it affects every setup where two people need to interact with the same system at once.

info-2.title: Each screen gets its own session
info-2.paragraph1: Duo Input handles each input source independently, at the system level, below any application.
info-2.paragraph2: Each screen gets its own input context. Both users interact freely. Neither interrupts the other.
info-2.paragraph3: It works across touchscreens and external displays. Nothing to configure. It just works.

info-3.title: The company that solved it
info-3.paragraph1: ID24 identified the Duo Input problem early, and built the solution from the ground up. Their technology is patented, deployed in real enterprise environments, and purpose-built for situations where two people share one system.
info-3.paragraph2: From retail terminals to medicing signing, wherever a second screen meets a second user, ID24 makes it work.
